question_text: An 8-year-old boy with asthma is brought to the physician because of a 2-week history of facial pain and congestion. His mother states that the nasal discharge was initially clear, but it has become thicker and more purulent over the last week. He has tried multiple over-the-counter oral decongestants and antihistamines, with minimal relief. Current medications include cetirizine, intranasal oxymetazoline, and albuterol. His temperature is 37.7°C (99.8°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows congested nasal mucosa with purulent discharge from the nares bilaterally. There is tenderness to palpation over the cheeks, with no transillumination over the maxillary sinuses. Which of the following is the most likely predisposing factor for this patient's current condition?
